caption: The drawing depicts a textile design composed of multiple rectangular sections filled with intricate patterns and motifs. The primary colors are dark blue, red, and off-white, creating strong contrasts. Floral and botanical elements dominate the design, with stylized flowers and leaves arranged symmetrically in some squares. Several vertically and horizontally aligned bands feature repeating geometric and star-like shapes. Near the bottom left, the text “YEAR 1854” is integrated into the pattern within two rectangular frames. Some sections are filled with a denser pattern of small flowers, while others have larger, more open motifs. The border along the bottom and left sides consists of alternating red and off-white geometric shapes resembling flowers or stars. The upper right corner contains a smaller rectangular inset with a grid of alternating blue and red squares, each filled with a detailed floral pattern surrounded by a blue border. The drawn textile includes a short fringe along the bottom edge, suggesting the end of a woven fabric. The overall composition is balanced with repeating elements and a clear division into separate yet related segments.
title: Woven Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
